rows.under: Leaves without a handoff. Open threads sit until they get back.
rows.justRight: Writes down what is in progress, who can make which calls, and the one kind of problem worth texting them about. The team keeps moving, and they actually rest.
rows.over: Stays on email and chat all week and overrides the calls their backup makes. The backup never really owns the work, and they come back already tired.

rows.under: Marks it done when the code is merged. Does not check whether the person who needed it can finish the job.
rows.justRight: Confirms the person who asked for it can actually use it. If something is left, they name an owner for it before they close the ticket.
rows.over: Leaves it open to chase extras nobody asked for. The work queued behind it waits.

rows.under: Ships the patch and walks away. The next person hits the same problem and finds no note explaining it.
rows.justRight: Ships the patch so people can keep working this week, then either schedules the real fix or writes down why the patch is good enough.
rows.over: Holds the release for a full rewrite. People wait on a problem that already had a safe patch.

rows.under: Watches the thread and adds nothing. The week slips while people wait for someone more senior to weigh in.
rows.justRight: Posts a recommendation, who gets hurt by waiting, and when they will go ahead if no one objects.
rows.over: Makes the call alone on something that commits other teams. The next few days go to undoing it.

rows.under: Treats launch day as the finish line. Docs, known bugs, and follow-ups have no name on them.
rows.justRight: Before the team scatters, they list what is left, what can wait, and who takes each piece.
rows.over: Will not call it launched until every leftover is gone. The start date for the next project moves.

rows.situation: Two teams started the same work
rows.under: Notices the overlap and keeps building their version. Two versions get built and one gets thrown out.
rows.justRight: Stops, compares scope, and picks which team finishes. The other team's time goes back to their plan.
rows.over: Takes over both efforts and rebuilds a combined version so they can be the owner. Both teams lose the week they already spent.

rows.under: Changes it for their case and ships. Other teams find out when their work breaks.
rows.justRight: Lists the teams that depend on it, gives them time to move, and keeps the old version working through this week.
rows.over: Waits until every team that depends on it has moved, even teams that never use the field being changed. A small fix sits while their own users stay blocked.

rows.under: Tells the customer it is not their promise. The customer is left with no next step.
rows.justRight: Takes the next call with the customer. They confirm what was promised, what can actually ship, and who will tell the customer.
rows.over: Honors a promise the team cannot keep so they look like the owner. Planned work for the week gets dropped.

rows.situation: A standing meeting that always runs long
rows.under: Lets the meeting keep the same shape. People stop preparing because nothing about it ever changes.
rows.justRight: Changes one part of the meeting this week, such as the timebox or the order, and watches the next few sessions before changing anything else. Protects the time the meeting is supposed to save.
rows.over: Redesigns the meeting every few days. The team spends more energy on the meeting format than on the work the meeting should unblock.

rows.situation: Handing work to the next person
rows.under: Passes a messy draft and assumes they will clean it up. The same gaps appear again one step later.
rows.justRight: Fixes the problems they would not want to inherit, and names the one risk that is still open. Leaves the next person real work, not a cleanup they did not plan for.
rows.over: Polishes every edge before anyone else can see it. The handoff is late, and the next person has no time left to react.

rows.situation: A workaround the team has used for months
rows.under: Treats the workaround as the real process. Never checks whether a cleaner path is now cheap enough to take.
rows.justRight: Keeps the workaround through this week's deadline, then makes a small change that removes one painful step. Does not wait for a full rewrite.
rows.over: Stops the week's delivery to replace the whole workaround. The original work slips, and the new path is only half built.

rows.under: Approves it to stay out of the way. Leaves known gaps for someone later to find.
rows.justRight: Flags the few issues that would hurt the reader or the next step, and lets the rest go. Says what the bar is so the next draft starts higher.
rows.over: Rewrites the draft in their own voice. The author spends the rest of the week arguing about wording, not fixing the substance that still needs work.

rows.situation: A problem that was fixed and came back
rows.under: Applies the same patch and moves on. Does not ask why the first fix did not hold.
rows.justRight: Gets things working again, then spends an hour or two on why the problem came back. Leaves a note so the next person does not repeat the quick fix.
rows.over: Opens a rewrite of the whole area. The original problem stays open longer, and other work waits on a redesign nobody needed this week.

rows.situation: Picking what to improve this week
rows.under: Says the team is too busy to change anything. Next week looks exactly like this one.
rows.justRight: Picks one thing that actually slowed the team down and makes a small change they can undo. Protects delivery time so the improvement does not become the project.
rows.over: Starts several improvement efforts at once. Meetings fill with process talk, and the customer-facing work slips.

rows.situation: Showing a new person the current process
rows.under: Walks them through the current steps as if they are finished. Does not name the rough edges or invite a better way.
rows.justRight: Teaches the path that works today and points out one place it still hurts. Asks them to try a small fix only after they can do the job.
rows.over: Hands the new person a redesign of the process in their first week. They cannot yet do the work, and the old path has no owner.

rows.under: Closes the ticket and does not look at what was clumsy in the final push. The same scramble will happen next time.
rows.justRight: Writes down one step that was harder than it needed to be and does a small cleanup while the memory is fresh. Does not reopen the whole release.
rows.over: Holds a long retrospective and starts a quality program. The next release waits while the team debates standards.

rows.under: Treats the ticket as the whole job. Does not ask what larger outcome the work is for.
rows.justRight: Names the larger outcome, then cuts this week to the smallest slice that tests it. The team can see the ambition and still finish something real by Friday.
rows.over: Inflates a one week ticket into a program before anyone has tried a small version. Nearby commitments slip while the plan grows.

rows.situation: A customer asks for a tweak
rows.under: Builds exactly the tweak and stops. Never asks whether the request points at a bigger gap.
rows.justRight: Ships a useful fix this week and writes down the larger need it hints at. The customer gets help now, and the team has a better idea of what to build next.
rows.over: Pauses the tweak to redesign the whole product around one request. The customer waits, and the team spends the week on a vision that nothing can test yet.

rows.under: The proposal only covers what the team already knows how to do. The request is safe and easy to forget.
rows.justRight: States a goal that would matter if it worked, then proposes a cheap first test. Reviewers can argue about both the ambition and the first step in the same meeting.
rows.over: The proposal is all vision and no first step. The room agrees with the vision and leaves with nothing to build this week.

rows.under: Treats headcount, tooling, or policy as immovable and shrinks the idea to fit. Nobody asks whether the constraint should change.
rows.justRight: Names the constraint, checks whether it is real, and either works around it or asks specifically for it to be lifted. The idea stays large enough to matter, and the request is specific enough to get an answer this week.
rows.over: Insists every constraint come off the table before any work starts. The team waits on permissions when a smaller test could have run.

rows.under: Reports only the task. Teammates cannot tell what larger bet the work belongs to.
rows.justRight: Ties today's task to the larger bet in one sentence, then says what will be true by Friday. People leave knowing the direction and what this week should prove.
rows.over: Uses standup to restate the long vision. The update runs long and nobody knows what is shipping.

rows.under: Approves a design that only clears the current ticket. Does not ask what happens if the bet actually works.
rows.justRight: Asks how the design would hold up if usage grew, then accepts a simpler first version if the path to that scale is clear. The author leaves with a small first version to build and knows which limit to plan for next.
rows.over: Rejects every simple design until it handles imagined future scale. The first version never ships, and the team keeps redrawing.

rows.under: Picks the safest test, the one that cannot change anyone's mind. The bigger question stays untouched.
rows.justRight: Chooses an experiment small enough to run this week that would change the larger bet if it failed. The team accepts a clear no in exchange for a clearer direction.
rows.over: Designs an experiment so large it needs new infrastructure first. The question that could have been answered this week waits.

rows.under: Notes the workaround and moves on. Treats it as a one-off instead of a signal of a larger unmet need.
rows.justRight: Eases the immediate pain, then spends an hour asking what people are really trying to get done with the workaround. A bigger opportunity gets named without dropping this week's work.
rows.over: Throws out the current plan to turn the workaround into the next big product. Focus scatters and committed work slips.

rows.situation: A thread that needs a decision
rows.under: Lets the thread sit. People keep adding comments instead of making a call.
rows.justRight: Names the decision, picks a reversible option with the information already in the thread, and writes what would change it.
rows.over: Closes the thread with a snap decision that ignores a constraint someone already raised there. The team spends the rest of the week undoing the work.

rows.under: Starts more research when the open questions would not change this week's action.
rows.justRight: Stops the research once it will not move the decision, starts the reversible work, and leaves a note on what is still unknown.
rows.over: Skips the afternoon of research that would have answered the one real risk. Someone else has to clean up the mistake.

rows.under: Waits for the owner to return before touching work that is stuck. Nothing moves for the week.
rows.justRight: Tries a cheap path that can be reversed, and tells the owner what they did.
rows.over: Forces a path the owner had already ruled out. The owner spends their first day back cleaning it up.

rows.under: Freezes until a new plan is approved. The remaining days are spent waiting.
rows.justRight: Picks a next step that is cheap to try and easy to reverse, and tells the people who were working on the old plan.
rows.over: Scraps the plan and starts a new one the same day without checking who is already partway through the old one. Their work no longer fits.

rows.under: Adds another review because it feels safer. The action waits for a slot that is not this week.
rows.justRight: Takes the review that would catch a mistake that is hard to undo, and skips the rest so the work can start.
rows.over: Skips the review that was going to catch a known risk. The people who would have flagged it find out after the cost is real.

rows.situation: A choice that can be undone
rows.under: Treats a reversible choice like a strategy decision. Days go to alignment the choice does not need.
rows.justRight: Picks one, starts, and watches. Changes it if the first days show it is wrong.
rows.over: Flips the choice twice in one week. People stop trusting the direction and redo work each time.

rows.situation: Work that is ready enough to share
rows.under: Holds the draft until it is polished. Reviewers have nothing to react to this week.
rows.justRight: Shares the rough version early enough that feedback can still change it, and says what is still unfinished.
rows.over: Sends half formed work to a wide list so it looks like progress. People spend time commenting on parts they already knew were wrong.

rows.situation: A small fix in front of you
rows.under: Files it for later and lives with the friction for the rest of the week.
rows.justRight: Fixes the reversible part now, and leaves a note if a larger change still needs a decision.
rows.over: Reworks the surrounding process in the same sitting. People who used the old path are surprised and lose time.

rows.situation: A customer is blocked this week
rows.under: Closes the ticket once it is assigned elsewhere. Does not check whether the customer can work again.
rows.justRight: Stays with the issue until the customer can continue. Pulls in whoever is needed, gives the customer a clear next step, and keeps the fix small enough that the rest of the week's work still ships.
rows.over: Camps on the ticket and drops the other customer work already in flight. Those customers wait while one issue gets undivided attention.

rows.under: Works the newest or easiest tickets. Bugs that stop customers from getting their work done sit in the backlog.
rows.justRight: Asks which defects are blocking real jobs this week. Fixes those first, even when they are messy, and leaves cosmetic issues with a short note on why they wait.
rows.over: Treats every small complaint as urgent. The team spends the week on one-off annoyances while a bug that blocks customers stays open.

rows.situation: Another team is waiting on you
rows.under: Leaves the request in the queue. Does not ask what customer work is stuck behind it.
rows.justRight: Learns who is blocked and what they need to finish this week. Sends a smaller first version that unblocks them and holds the extras for later, so both teams' customer work can move.
rows.over: Drops their own customer commitments to polish the internal request past what was asked. The asking team gets more than they needed, and external customers wait.

rows.under: Walks through internal plans. Leaves without knowing what the customer is trying to get done.
rows.justRight: Starts by asking what the customer is working on and what is in the way. Commits only to what the team can do soon, writes it down, and takes the rest back as input rather than a promise.
rows.over: Says yes to every request to keep the meeting warm. The team spends the following days untangling commitments it cannot staff.

rows.situation: A promised date is going to slip
rows.under: Stays silent. The customer learns about the miss when the work does not arrive.
rows.justRight: Calls as soon as the slip is certain. Offers a smaller piece they can use now and a date for the rest that the team can actually hold.
rows.over: Adds free extras or a tighter new date to soften the news. The second miss costs more trust than the first honest delay would have.

rows.situation: One customer asks for a custom change
rows.under: Parks the request and never checks whether anyone else has the same problem.
rows.justRight: Asks how widespread the need is. Builds a shared version if it is common, or declines the one-off and offers a path the product already supports.
rows.over: Squeezes the special case into this week's work. Support now has to handle an exception, and the next customer expects the same treatment.

rows.situation: Reviewing a change before it ships
rows.under: Marks the ticket done without walking the customer path. Confusing steps go out unnoticed.
rows.justRight: Tries the change the way a customer will. Holds the release for a step that would block them, and lets leftover polish wait until after it ships.
rows.over: Stops the release over minor wording and rare edge cases. The fix customers are waiting on sits another week.

rows.under: Avoids the conversation. The customer keeps planning around something the team will not build.
rows.justRight: States the no, the reason, and what saying yes would cost other customers. Offers the closest supported option and puts the answer in writing, including what would have to change for the team to reconsider.
rows.over: Softens the no until it sounds like a later yes. The customer staffs a plan around a capability that never arrives.

rows.situation: A weekly status that is all green
rows.under: Treats the green boxes as the update. Does not open a single item to see the work behind it.
rows.justRight: Samples the two or three items that would hurt next week if they were false, traces those to the actual work, and leaves the rest once the sample holds.
rows.over: Questions every line until the owner spends the next day rebuilding the status report instead of doing the work.

rows.situation: A teammate says they already checked
rows.under: Accepts the assurance and never looks at the source they used.
rows.justRight: Asks to see the source once, confirms the check was real, and then lets them own the next ones.
rows.over: Rechecks their work in the room every time. They stop checking themselves because it will be redone anyway.

rows.under: Signs because the amount looks familiar or the requester is trusted. Does not open the quote.
rows.justRight: Reads the quote and the alternatives, asks the one or two questions that could change the decision, and then signs or sends it back.
rows.over: Rebuilds the vendor comparison from scratch and holds the order. The team misses the window they needed the thing for.

rows.under: Accepts the summary email and never opens the docs or code being handed over.
rows.justRight: Reads the docs and code their team will need this week, names the gaps that would stall them, and then lets the handoff go.
rows.over: Rewrites the other team's docs and code before accepting the handoff. Both teams wait on a cleanup that was not in the plan.

rows.under: Marks lines done from memory. Does not look at the test results or dashboards behind each item.
rows.justRight: Verifies the few items that would hurt customers if they were false, then ships on the rest of the list.
rows.over: Makes the team rerun every test and walk through every item on the list live, including ones already checked. The launch window closes while the team redoes work that was already finished.

rows.under: Repeats the vendor's number in the internal update. Does not compare it to our own records.
rows.justRight: Checks the claim against a week of our own records, names any gap, and then decides whether to keep the vendor, push back, or drop them.
rows.over: Starts an audit of the vendor's whole history before the next call. The renewal or the switch to a new vendor sits while the audit keeps growing.

rows.situation: A message asking for a quick approval
rows.under: Replies yes without opening the attachment.
rows.justRight: Opens the attachment, checks the part that cannot be undone, and answers the same day.
rows.over: Holds the message overnight to reread the whole thread. The person who needed the approval misses their deadline.

rows.under: Takes the new date and does not look at what actually stalled.
rows.justRight: Traces the slip to the real blocker, names it, and resets only what that blocker requires.
rows.over: Audits the whole plan from the first task. The team spends the week explaining history instead of clearing the blocker.

rows.under: Lets the day pass and hopes no one notices. The other person finds out when they chase the work.
rows.justRight: Flags the slip as soon as it is real, says what still holds, and offers a new date they can keep. Owns the miss once, then gets back to the work.
rows.over: Sends a long apology and keeps asking if people are still disappointed. The delivery waits while the relationship gets managed.

rows.under: Tells the story as if the call was mostly theirs. Teammates hear their names late or not at all.
rows.justRight: Names who did the hard parts in the review, and still owns the outcome if something breaks later.
rows.over: Deflects every compliment so thoroughly that no one can tell who decided what. Reviewers leave unsure who is accountable.

rows.situation: Asked something you do not know
rows.under: Answers with confidence anyway. The gap shows up later in the work.
rows.justRight: Says what they know, what they do not, and when they will come back with the rest. People can plan around the gap.
rows.over: Prefaces every answer with how little they know. The meeting stalls because no one will take a position.

rows.situation: A gap in a peer's draft
rows.under: Stays quiet to keep things easy. The issue ships with their name next to the review.
rows.justRight: Takes the concern to the person first, with the specific evidence, and stays open if they have context the reviewer lacked.
rows.over: Raises it on a wide email thread to show they caught it. The peer spends the week defending the draft instead of fixing it.

rows.under: Softens the update until the risk is hard to read. The stakeholder learns the truth from the outcome.
rows.justRight: States the miss, the impact, and the next step in the same note. Does not pad it, and does not dump it without a path.
rows.over: Leads every update with everything that might go wrong. People stop paying attention because every update sounds like an alarm.

rows.situation: You were wrong in a review
rows.under: Lets the written comment stand. People keep building on a view they already know is off.
rows.justRight: Corrects themselves in the same review thread, briefly, and updates the decision. Takes the awkward minute so the written record is right.
rows.over: Replays the miss in later meetings. The team spends more time on the apology than on the new call.

rows.situation: A newer teammate flags a risk
rows.under: Waves it off because the person is new. The risk sits unexamined.
rows.justRight: Hears them out, checks the claim, and credits the flag if it holds. Pushes back with reasons if it does not, so they still bring the next one.
rows.over: Treats every new concern as equally urgent. Nobody weighs which ones matter, and the list fills with noise.

rows.under: Talks as if this team is already the standard. No one looks at stronger work nearby.
rows.justRight: Puts this week's work next to a stronger example, without shaming the people who built it. Uses the gap to pick one thing to raise this week.
rows.over: Compares the team to a famous team somewhere else so often that people stop believing the comparison. Energy goes into feeling behind, not into the next fix.

rows.under: Sits through the review and saves the real objection for the hallway. The room leaves thinking there is alignment.
rows.justRight: Names the specific risk while the owner can still change course, and offers a smaller test or a narrower change. Once the owner decides, writes up the decision as settled, not as another round of debate.
rows.over: Relitigates last week's same point in every review. People stop sending this person the doc in time, and the design lands later than it needed to.

rows.under: Goes along with the go to keep the call short, even though a known issue is still open.
rows.justRight: Holds if the open issue would actually hurt the customer, and says what would flip the vote. After the owner calls it, does the assigned launch work and does not seed doubt in the launch channel.
rows.over: Blocks the launch on a preference that can wait. The team stays late for a fight that did not have to be tonight.

rows.under: Withdraws and does the chosen work at half effort. The team can tell the commit is not real.
rows.justRight: Makes the case once with the evidence that mattered, then builds the chosen path as if it were theirs. Flags only new facts, not the same pitch in a new wrapper.
rows.over: Keeps a side version of the old idea running. Attention splits, and whoever is waiting on one plan gets two half answers.

rows.under: Lets a weak plan lock because no one else spoke. Next week the team is stuck executing it.
rows.justRight: Breaks the silence with the concrete problem and a workable alternative. Stops once the owner has enough to decide, even if the room is still uncomfortable.
rows.over: Fills every pause with another objection. The meeting never closes, and people leave without knowing what to do on Monday.

rows.under: Goes along with a hire they do not think can do the job. The concern never makes the notes.
rows.justRight: States the specific gap and how it would show up in the first month of the job. Votes, then honors the group's call and helps the person land if they join.
rows.over: Relitigates the candidate after the offer is out. The loop loses a week, and the candidate feels the delay.

rows.under: Presents the summary deck as if it belongs to someone else, or sends someone else so they do not have to defend the plan.
rows.justRight: Presents the chosen plan as the team's plan and keeps the real risks on the table as watch items. Does not use the stage to reopen the vote.
rows.over: Uses the presentation to argue the old case one more time. The audience leaves unsure what was decided, and the team loses a day re-explaining the call.

rows.under: Stays silent while others walk the decision back in the thread. By Friday the plan has two versions.
rows.justRight: If the facts are unchanged, restates the decision and the next step. If something material changed, asks the owner to reopen it in the right forum, not in the chat.
rows.over: Argues the same point across three channels. People mute the thread, and the work sits until next week's meeting.

rows.situation: A peer's proposal creates work for you
rows.under: Nods in the meeting and later says the team cannot take it. The proposer has already promised dates.
rows.justRight: Challenges the proposal while it is still a proposal, with the real cost and a smaller version that would work. Once it is in, staffs it without a second campaign against it.
rows.over: Treats every incoming ask as a fight to win. Peers stop bringing work early, and the team learns about commitments after they are already public.

rows.under: Sits through the debrief and agrees with the loudest interviewer. Never says whether this person would be stronger than the people already on the team.
rows.justRight: Compares the candidate, skill by skill, to people already doing the work. Votes no when the hire would only fill a seat, even if the team is tired of covering.
rows.over: Treats every mixed signal as a no. Strong candidates stall, interviewers stop trusting the process, and the team keeps covering the open work.

rows.situation: A teammate asks to move internally
rows.under: Changes the subject when they ask about other teams. Holds onto them because this quarter's plan needs them where they are.
rows.justRight: Helps them find a role that uses what they already do well, then plans a handoff so current work does not fall over.
rows.over: Walks them to the new team the same week to look generous. The remaining people inherit undocumented work and a hole in coverage.

rows.under: Runs through tickets and deadlines. Growth never makes the agenda.
rows.justRight: Spends part of the hour on one skill to practice this week and the rest on the work in front of them. The person leaves with a next step that fits the current load.
rows.over: Turns the meeting into a weekly career workshop. Delivery slips, and the person spends more time being coached than doing the work.

rows.under: Moves the friend to the front of the line and softens written feedback so the colleague is not embarrassed.
rows.justRight: Runs the same loop and the same standard as any other candidate. Tells the colleague the outcome without dressing it up.
rows.over: Adds extra interviews to prove there was no favoritism. The candidate takes another offer while the loop is still running.

rows.under: Gives the work to whoever has done it before. Everyone else stays in their lane.
rows.justRight: Puts a less experienced person on it with enough cover that the customer still gets a solid result. Names what they should learn by Friday.
rows.over: Hands them the critical path with no backup so they can grow. The date slips, and they spend the next month repairing trust.

rows.under: Screens for keywords that match the people already on the team. Unusual backgrounds never get a loop.
rows.justRight: Advances people who could do the work the team will need next year, even when their titles do not match. Passes on a comfortable lookalike who would only add a pair of hands.
rows.over: Advances anyone who looks impressive on paper. Interviewers spend the week on people who cannot do the job, and the candidates who could are still waiting.

rows.under: Hands them a laptop and the backlog. They copy whatever they see, including sloppy habits.
rows.justRight: Gives them real work and a named person to learn from. Checks that they are picking up the standard, not just the tools.
rows.over: Fills the calendar with shadowing and reading lists. They produce nothing, and the team still carries their load.

rows.under: Presents it themselves every time. The people who did the work stay unknown outside the team.
rows.justRight: Lets the person who did the work present, and steps in only for gaps. Uses the room to coach without taking the credit.
rows.over: Puts someone unready in front of a high-stakes audience with no rehearsal. Their reputation takes the hit, and the work looks weaker than it is.

rows.under: Waves it off because it did not start here. The team keeps building its own copy of something that already works next door.
rows.justRight: Gives the idea a real look even when the source is unexpected. Takes what fits this problem and invents only the part that is still missing.
rows.over: Copies the other team's whole approach without checking the fit. People spend the week bending a solution that was built for a different job.

rows.situation: Extra steps on a request form
rows.under: Leaves every field and approval in place. Requesters keep filling out details nobody reads.
rows.justRight: Sits with a few recent requests and removes the fields that never change a decision. Keeps the two or three questions that still catch a real miss.
rows.over: Cuts the form to almost nothing. Reviewers have to chase people for context, and the queue slows down for everyone.

rows.under: Pulls the prototype when the room looks confused. The team goes back to the familiar design so no one has to sit with something new.
rows.justRight: Walks through what the prototype is trying to make simpler and names what is still unproven. Leaves it in play long enough to get one concrete reaction from the people who would use it.
rows.over: Treats every objection as proof the room just does not get it. Review time runs out, and the people who have to live with the change stop offering useful pushback.

rows.under: Cuts it off because it is not ready. People learn to bring only finished thoughts, and the half formed ones never show up.
rows.justRight: Gives the idea a few minutes and asks what pain it would remove. Either parks it with a next step or says why this week is the wrong time.
rows.over: Turns every passing idea into a chat thread or a research task. Standup runs long, and the work that was already on the board loses the morning.

rows.situation: Scope on a ticket this week
rows.under: Implements the request exactly as written. Adds another screen and another setting when a smaller change would have removed the same friction.
rows.justRight: Checks what the person is trying to finish and ships the smallest change that unblocks them. Writes down what was left out so it does not vanish.
rows.over: Trims the ticket so far that the original pain is still there. The requester opens a follow-up, and the team touches the same area twice.

rows.under: Does the same hand edit again and treats it as normal. No one looks for a simpler way to make the patch unnecessary.
rows.justRight: Does the patch so this week's delivery still goes out, and names a simpler fix with an owner. Comes back to it before the patch becomes the official path.
rows.over: Halts the delivery to build a clean replacement right away. The thing people are waiting on slips while the team builds something nobody needed this week.

rows.situation: A repetitive task that eats the afternoon
rows.under: Clicks through the same steps again and treats that as the work. Nobody asks whether the middle can go away.
rows.justRight: Automates the boring middle and keeps a person checking any step where a wrong answer would reach a customer. The task takes less time next week, and the risk is still visible.
rows.over: Scripts the whole path, including the judgment call. When the odd case shows up, the afternoon goes to untangling a tool no one else can read.

rows.under: Hides the draft until it looks finished. The demo is a slide deck, and no one has actually tried the thing.
rows.justRight: Shows the rough cut and says what is still missing. Gets a reaction on the simple path before the design is locked.
rows.over: Demos every half built idea as if it is already the plan. People leave confused about what is real, and the next few days go to resetting expectations.

rows.situation: An unfamiliar term in a meeting
rows.under: Lets the term pass so the meeting can move. Stays lost for the rest of the discussion.
rows.justRight: Asks a brief question or notes it and looks it up the same day. Comes back only if it changes the work.
rows.over: Stops the meeting for a full explainer. The agenda does not finish, and people stay late to recover the decisions.

rows.situation: A new library that might help this week
rows.under: Ignores it and stays on the familiar path even when that path is slow.
rows.justRight: Gives the library a short, time boxed try. Keeps the old path if the try does not clearly help this ticket.
rows.over: Rebuilds the whole task around the library. The original work slips while they compare options.

rows.under: Skips it because the service is not theirs. Misses a change that will land on them.
rows.justRight: Reads the doc, attends if it touches their work, and asks a question that tests one assumption. Leaves when the rest is not their problem.
rows.over: Sits in every review and debates each design. Their own tickets wait.

rows.under: Keeps forcing the same method. Does not read, ask, or try another path.
rows.justRight: Pauses, looks up how others solved it, and tries one different approach with a time box. Returns to the original if the detour is worse.
rows.over: Drops the ticket to survey every method they can find. Days pass with nothing working in the branch.

rows.under: Leaves it for the specialist. Does not open the docs or attempt a first cut.
rows.justRight: Takes the ticket, learns the part it needs, and checks with someone who knows the area before merging.
rows.over: Uses the ticket as a reason to study the whole stack. The ticket sits while they take a course.

rows.situation: Data that does not match the plan
rows.under: Talks past the numbers so the plan can stay. Does not open the raw source.
rows.justRight: Pulls the data, names what they do not understand, and changes the plan only where the evidence is clear.
rows.over: Rewrites the whole plan from one surprising chart. The team chases a new theory each afternoon.

rows.situation: A question you cannot answer in your own review
rows.under: Bluffs or shuts the question down so they still look like the expert.
rows.justRight: Says they do not know, writes the question down, and comes back after they have checked. Keeps the review moving.
rows.over: Turns the review into a live research session. Reviewers sit while they read docs on the call.

rows.situation: Someone asks why we do it this way
rows.under: Answers "that is how we do it" and moves on. Does not check whether the reason still holds.
rows.justRight: Explains the history, admits the parts they are unsure about, and looks it up if the answer may be stale. Changes the practice only if that check warrants it.
rows.over: Turns the question into a rewrite of the team's process. Shipping pauses for a long debate.

rows.under: Starts new work and leaves the Monday item sitting. The person waiting finds out only when they ask.
rows.justRight: Finishes it or names a new date before picking up the next thing. Says what will wait and who needs to know.
rows.over: Keeps reworking every old item until each one is perfect. Time-sensitive work waits.

rows.under: Stops and waits for a cleaner plan or a new owner. The original date stays on the calendar.
rows.justRight: Tries another path the same day and tells the people waiting what changed. Keeps the outcome and drops the method that failed.
rows.over: Spends the rest of the week forcing the first approach. Neighboring work sits, and the date still moves.

rows.situation: Calling a piece of work done
rows.under: Marks it done while the handoff, check, or last user step is still open. The next person finds the holes.
rows.justRight: Confirms someone can actually use it, then stops. Leaves small nits only when they do not block use, and writes them down.
rows.over: Refuses to close until every nit is gone. People who needed it wait while it keeps getting touched.

rows.situation: Two deadlines in the same week
rows.under: Works whichever is louder and lets the other slip with no notice.
rows.justRight: Chooses the one that matters more, tells the other stakeholder what will move, and finishes the first one so it can be used.
rows.over: Promises both will land and splits the week so thin that neither result is usable.

rows.under: Adds it without moving anything already promised. Both pieces start to slip.
rows.justRight: Weighs it against this week's commitments. Takes it only if something else is deferred out loud, or if the new work is truly small.
rows.over: Protects the original list so tightly that a small, time-sensitive ask waits a week for no real reason.

rows.situation: Giving status when the work is behind
rows.under: Stays quiet or still says on track. The slip appears only when the date arrives.
rows.justRight: Says what is late, what will still land this week, and what they need. Gives others time to react.
rows.over: Sends frequent updates that restate the same risk. People spend the week reading status instead of unblocking the work.

rows.under: Waits for every input to be clean before starting. The date does not move, and the week goes by.
rows.justRight: Starts with what is in hand, marks the assumptions, and adjusts when the rest arrives.
rows.over: Builds a full answer on guesses so they can say they started. The real inputs arrive and the week is spent redoing it.

rows.under: Does not reset the plan. The miss goes unexplained, and the next date is just as soft.
rows.justRight: Says what slipped, why, and the new date they will actually hit. Cuts scope if that is what makes the new date real.
rows.over: Names a tight catch-up date to repair the miss. The following week starts already behind.

rows.under: Asks for more people before looking at scope or reuse. Headcount is the first lever.
rows.justRight: Trims what this cycle does not need and reuses what already works. Adds help only when the remaining work is more than the current team can finish, and new people can start in time.
rows.over: Turns down every extra person to keep the team small. The same few people absorb the slip, they stay late, and the date still moves.

rows.under: Takes the first quote. Does not check what the team can do itself or whether a cheaper option covers the need.
rows.justRight: Compares a short list against the real need, including doing the work in house. Pays more only when the cheap path will create rework or a lock-in later.
rows.over: Takes the lowest bid even when the vendor cannot do the job. The team spends the following week fixing or replacing what came back.

rows.under: Spends the remainder so next year's number does not shrink. Buys things the team does not need this quarter.
rows.justRight: Returns what will not be used well. Spends only on things that would have been bought anyway, and writes down what next year actually needs.
rows.over: Holds back spend that is already justified, to look careful. Materials or licenses arrive late, and the next month starts with a scramble.

rows.situation: Another team already built something close
rows.under: Starts from scratch because the existing thing is not a perfect fit. The week goes into rebuilding what already shipped.
rows.justRight: Adapts the existing work where it fits, and builds only the gap. Accepts a few rough edges instead of a second system to maintain.
rows.over: Forces the old thing onto a problem it cannot serve. People spend more time fighting the mismatch than a small new build would have taken.

rows.under: Puts the full vision into the first cut. The week fills with extras no one needed this cycle.
rows.justRight: Ships the smallest version that can be used and judged, and parks the rest. Puts leftover time into the one piece that would be expensive to change later.
rows.over: Cuts so far that the result cannot be used or tested. The same slice has to be rebuilt the following week.

rows.situation: A teammate needs a small purchase
rows.under: Buys without checking whether a shared option already exists. Duplicate kits and licenses collect on desks.
rows.justRight: Checks what the team already has, then buys the cheapest thing that will hold up for the job. Does not send people hunting for a free workaround that eats the afternoon.
rows.over: Makes people use a broken spare or a clumsy free tool. The task takes the rest of the day, and the savings are gone.

rows.situation: Hiring a contractor for a short job
rows.under: Brings in outside help for work the team could finish with a small scope cut. The invoice covers hours that were never scarce.
rows.justRight: Uses a contractor when the skill is missing and the deadline is real. Keeps the scope of work tight so the team still owns the result and does not pay for idle time.
rows.over: Refuses outside help to avoid the fee. The only person who can do the work is already booked, so the launch waits.

rows.situation: An order will miss the date
rows.under: Pays rush fees on every slip without checking whether the original day still matters. Rush shipping becomes the default.
rows.justRight: Expedites only when a miss is real and costly. For the rest, resets the date and stays on the standard path.
rows.over: Refuses every rush charge. A customer who needed that day is left waiting, and the team spends the next week on recovery.

rows.situation: Handing work to the next team
rows.under: Sends the work with known gaps and lets the next team find them.
rows.justRight: Fixes the issues that would become someone else's defects, and names what is still open. Leaves polish that would delay the handoff more than it helps.
rows.over: Holds the work until every edge case is clean. The next team waits and the shared date moves.

rows.under: Applies last week's patch again and closes the ticket.
rows.justRight: Fixes the symptom and changes the check or step that let it through, even if that costs another day this week.
rows.over: Stops the team's other work to redesign around one returning bug. Commitments for the rest of the week slip.

rows.under: Skims and approves so the author can stay on the calendar.
rows.justRight: Calls out the few places that would actually lower the bar, and says why. Leaves wording nits that do not change the outcome.
rows.over: Rewrites the draft in their own voice. The author stops owning it, and the draft sits in review for the rest of the week.

rows.situation: The team says the bar is too high
rows.under: Drops the standard so the argument ends.
rows.justRight: Keeps the parts a customer would notice, and cuts scope or sequence so the team can still hit that bar this week.
rows.over: Treats every objection as a lack of will and refuses to cut anything. People work late and the work still ships late.

rows.under: Marks it done while a known defect is still in it for the next person to find.
rows.justRight: Fixes what would travel downstream, writes down the leftover risk, and only then closes it.
rows.over: Leaves the ticket open for cosmetic leftovers no customer will see. The board fills with work that is already good enough.

rows.situation: A new person ships their first work
rows.under: Lets them send it out without showing what done looks like on this team.
rows.justRight: Walks through one recent example of the standard and reviews their first piece against it, while still letting them finish the week.
rows.over: Makes them redo the first task until it matches a senior's taste in every detail. They lose the week and still cannot tell which parts matter.

rows.situation: A partner team's deliverable is rough
rows.under: Takes it as-is to keep the relationship easy.
rows.justRight: Sends it back with the specific gaps that would turn into defects here, and a way to land it this week.
rows.over: Rejects the whole deliverable and rebuilds it themselves. The partner stops trying, and this team now owns the partner's work.

rows.situation: A process already works but creates rework
rows.under: Leaves the clumsy step alone because it has not failed loudly this week.
rows.justRight: Tightens the one step that keeps producing rework, and leaves the rest until that change sticks.
rows.over: Redesigns the whole process in the same week. People spend their time learning new steps instead of doing the work.

rows.under: Treats rank as the argument and keeps the original call.
rows.justRight: Lets the fact win in the room, says what changed, and moves the decision.
rows.over: Opens a second debate after the fact is already in, so the team leaves with no call.

rows.under: Takes the agreement as proof and locks the path.
rows.justRight: Asks who would bet against it, and what evidence would change the call, before locking it.
rows.over: Keeps hunting dissent after a real objection has been answered, and the work waits.

rows.situation: A question the data can settle
rows.under: Runs the meeting on opinions when a test or the arithmetic would settle it.
rows.justRight: Runs the test or does the math, and uses judgment only for the part that remains.
rows.over: Refuses to decide the leftover until every unknown is gone, including ones that do not change the call.

rows.under: Hopes nobody notices, or defends the old call so it still looks consistent.
rows.justRight: Says the miss in the same week, names the better path, and switches to it.
rows.over: Spends the week narrating the miss and does not make the next call.

rows.situation: A hunch after the fact showed up
rows.under: Drops the hunch at the first objection and asks someone else to decide.
rows.justRight: Names the hunch, the fact that cuts against it, and which one the decision now follows.
rows.over: Keeps the hunch after the fact has cut it down, and calls that instinct.

rows.situation: Defending the plan you already announced
rows.under: Treats the announcement as the reason to stay, and argues with the new evidence.
rows.justRight: Updates the plan in public and says which assumption was wrong.
rows.over: Reverses the plan on every new comment, so nobody can tell which evidence mattered.

rows.under: Lets the room go personal, or goes quiet so the tension will pass.
rows.justRight: Names the miss, asks the person closest to it what they see, and ends with a next step people can say out loud.
rows.over: Gives a lecture about culture while the actual problem sits untouched.

rows.situation: Credit for work without the title
rows.under: Tells the story as if the senior person did the work.
rows.justRight: Says who did it, what was hard, and what the team should copy, in the room that matters.
rows.over: Stages a ceremony that embarrasses the person and skips the work itself.

rows.situation: A joke that lands on one person
rows.under: Laughs along, or waits to see if the person will object.
rows.justRight: Stops it in the moment, checks on the person, and says that kind of joke is not how this team works.
rows.over: Turns the correction into a long public scolding and the original work is lost.

rows.under: Treats recovery and morale as private matters and schedules the same hours again.
rows.justRight: Thanks people for the specific work, protects a real pause, and changes the plan so the same crush is not the default.
rows.over: Throws a celebration while the broken thing is still broken and calls that culture.

rows.under: Reviews the senior person's work carefully and waves the junior person's work through, or the reverse.
rows.justRight: Uses the same bar and the same straight feedback regardless of title.
rows.over: Holds the junior person's work to a performance so the review itself becomes the point.

rows.under: Waits for a survey, a poster, or another team to fix the room.
rows.justRight: Treats the room as part of this week's job and fixes the one behavior that made it worse.
rows.over: Builds a culture program and stops doing the management the room actually needed.

rows.under: Decides why they failed before asking what they saw.
rows.justRight: Asks what happened, restates it back, and only then says what should change.
rows.over: Interviews so long that the miss has no owner and no next step.

rows.under: Treats the disagreement as a verdict on the person.
rows.justRight: Stays on the work, gives the other view a fair hearing, and still makes the call.
rows.over: Avoids the disagreement so thoroughly that the team cannot tell what was decided.

rows.situation: Trust after you caused the miss
rows.under: Explains why it was not really yours and moves on.
rows.justRight: Owns the miss, says what you will do differently, and follows through on that small promise.
rows.over: Over-apologizes for days and leaves the repair to someone else.

rows.under: Asks for input and then repeats the answer you walked in with.
rows.justRight: Listens long enough to be able to change the answer, and says so if you do not.
rows.over: Refuses to close because someone in the room might still feel unheard.

rows.under: Points at the other team and waits.
rows.justRight: Takes your piece of it, says what you need from them, and does not make them carry your share.
rows.over: Takes the whole miss, including the parts you do not understand, and crowds them out of the repair.

rows.situation: Respect that never says the problem
rows.under: Says the harsh version in the hallway afterward.
rows.justRight: Says the problem to the person, plainly, and keeps the relationship intact enough to keep working.
rows.over: Softens the problem until they leave thinking everything is fine.

rows.situation: A person ready for harder work
rows.under: Keeps the hard piece because it is faster if you do it.
rows.justRight: Gives them the piece, stays close enough to catch a real miss, and lets them own the result.
rows.over: Hands over the whole area in one week and disappears.

rows.under: Names only the star, or only yourself.
rows.justRight: Names what the group did and the specific growth you saw in more than one person.
rows.over: Spreads the credit so evenly that nobody can tell what to do again.

rows.situation: One person wants every hard problem
rows.under: Lets them take all of it because the result will be better this week.
rows.justRight: Gives them a hard piece and gives the next one to someone who needs the practice.
rows.over: Benches the strong person to make a point, and the work suffers for the lesson.

rows.under: Offers it only to the person who already looks like the last person who had it.
rows.justRight: Says what the chance is, what good looks like, and invites more than one person to make a case.
rows.over: Rotates the chance so mechanically that the work has no owner who can succeed at it.

rows.under: Rewrites their work after hours and tells them it was fine.
rows.justRight: Shows them the gap, lets them fix it, and checks the result.
rows.over: Turns every task into a lesson and the delivery date slips for the teaching.

rows.under: Has no growth in the plan at all, only this week's tickets.
rows.justRight: Picks one stretch that still lets the week's commitment ship.
rows.over: Builds a development plan that replaces the job the team was hired to do.

rows.under: Recites a slogan and cannot say what it changes in this week's work.
rows.justRight: Says the strategy in their own words and points at the one decision it should change today.
rows.over: Rewrites the strategy in the hallway so it matches the project they already wanted.

rows.situation: A task that does not connect
rows.under: Does the task because it was assigned and never asks what it serves.
rows.justRight: Asks what outcome it moves, and drops or reshapes it when the answer is nothing.
rows.over: Drops assigned work they dislike and calls the preference the mission.

rows.under: Moves the number and does not notice the product got worse for the people who use it.
rows.justRight: Knows which number matters and checks that the product still does the job the strategy named.
rows.over: Ignores a number the strategy depends on because they prefer the craft of the product.

rows.situation: Impact you cannot see from your desk
rows.under: Cares about the work in front of them and treats the rest of the mission as someone else's.
rows.justRight: Goes and looks at the impact, then brings one concrete change back to the team.
rows.over: Spends the week touring the impact and does not finish the work that would change it.

rows.under: Dismisses the stack, the product, or the customer problem because it is not their specialty.
rows.justRight: Learns enough to care about the outcome and to ask a useful question of the people who own it.
rows.over: Becomes a second owner of the technology and crowds out the people who already know it.

rows.under: Waits to be told why the work matters and stays lukewarm until then.
rows.justRight: Brings energy to the agreed strategy, including the parts that are not the most interesting.
rows.over: Chases the part they love and lets the agreed plan stall.

rows.situation: A decision that touches another team
rows.under: Decides inside the function and tells the other team after it has shipped.
rows.justRight: Learns how the decision lands on them, then makes the call without waiting for every vote.
rows.over: Will not decide until every adjacent team has agreed, and the week is gone.

rows.situation: A dependency you do not own
rows.under: Treats the other team's queue as none of your business until you are blocked.
rows.justRight: Says what you need, what they are carrying, and a smaller slice that unblocks both sides.
rows.over: Takes over their work so you do not have to depend on them.

rows.situation: A meeting of only your function
rows.under: Solves a cross-team problem with the people who already share your view.
rows.justRight: Brings in the person who will live with the result, hears them, and still leaves with a decision.
rows.over: Invites so many functions that the meeting cannot decide anything.

rows.under: Equates disagreement with a failed collaboration and forces a watered-down middle.
rows.justRight: Understands the other view, states the disagreement, and decides.
rows.over: Calls a solo decision collaboration because you sent a note afterward.

rows.under: Optimizes the function and is surprised by what breaks downstream.
rows.justRight: Draws the two or three connections that matter for this decision and checks them.
rows.over: Maps the whole company before a local call that only one other team feels.

rows.under: Agrees in the meeting and undoes it back inside the function.
rows.justRight: Carries the decision back, including the part your own team did not prefer.
rows.over: Polices the other team all week to prove you are collaborating.

rows.under: Hires the first acceptable person so the seat is no longer empty.
rows.justRight: Holds the bar, keeps looking, and says what the team still needs that it does not have.
rows.over: Holds the seat empty for a perfect hire while the team cannot do the job in front of it.

rows.under: Skips the hard note to keep the relationship comfortable.
rows.justRight: Gives the specific gap and the specific strength, and asks for the same in return.
rows.over: Delivers only criticism and calls the volume a high bar.

rows.under: Lets the same two people decide and treats silence as agreement.
rows.justRight: Asks the quiet person for the view the room is missing, then uses it or says why not.
rows.over: Runs the meeting as a tour of every voice and never reaches a decision.

rows.under: Protects a teammate from feedback the team can already see.
rows.justRight: Supports the person and still names the gap in the work.
rows.over: Removes every hard assignment so nobody feels pressure, and the team stops growing.

rows.under: Staffs heroes and hopes the sum appears.
rows.justRight: Pairs people so the work needs more than one strength, and judges the result as a team.
rows.over: Blends roles so thoroughly that nobody is accountable for a piece.

rows.situation: A high bar that becomes a club
rows.under: Lowers the bar to keep the current group comfortable.
rows.justRight: Keeps the bar and makes the path onto the team legible to people who are not already inside it.
rows.over: Uses the bar to exclude people who work differently, and calls the sameness excellence.

rows.situation: A plan that does not add up
rows.under: Lets it pass because challenging it would slow the room.
rows.justRight: Says what does not make sense, listens, and drives a decision before the meeting ends.
rows.over: Keeps challenging after the decision so the work cannot start.

rows.situation: You see it differently from the room
rows.under: Goes along and saves the objection for later.
rows.justRight: Puts the independent view on the table, hears the reply, and either updates or holds it.
rows.over: Treats independent thinking as refusing to hear anyone else.

rows.situation: The room wants to keep talking
rows.under: Lets the discussion replace the decision.
rows.justRight: Summarizes the options, picks one, and names when you will revisit it.
rows.over: Cuts off the discussion before the objection has been understood.

rows.under: Drops the point as soon as you notice you are alone.
rows.justRight: States it once, clearly, and then commits to whatever the decision is.
rows.over: Reopens it with each new audience so the decision never settles.

rows.situation: A call that can be made today
rows.under: Asks for another meeting because the topic feels important.
rows.justRight: Decides today on the part that is clear and writes down the one question that can wait.
rows.over: Decides in the first minute and skips the listening the principle requires.

rows.under: Abandons a sound objection the moment a senior person frowns.
rows.justRight: Holds the objection while it still has a reason, and drops it when the reason is answered.
rows.over: Holds it after the reason is gone, and calls that backbone.

rows.under: Leaves it in because it has always been there.
rows.justRight: Removes it, watches the next few runs, and puts it back only if something real breaks.
rows.over: Removes a step that exists because a constraint cannot move, and finds out in production.

rows.situation: A side effort that is interesting
rows.under: Keeps it alive because the team enjoys it.
rows.justRight: Stops it and puts the time back on the thing that matters this quarter.
rows.over: Kills a required obligation because it is not the interesting goal.

rows.under: Treats every constraint as optional friction.
rows.justRight: Names the ones that cannot move, simplifies around them, and does not pretend they are gone.
rows.over: Adds process to honor the constraint in three places when one check would do.

rows.under: Keeps producing it for an audience that no longer reads it.
rows.justRight: Asks who decides from it, cuts the rest, and shortens what remains.
rows.over: Deletes the one figure the decision actually needs.

rows.under: Tries to move every item a little and finishes none of what matters.
rows.justRight: Picks the work that matters, finishes that, and explicitly drops the rest for this week.
rows.over: Drops so much that a real commitment with a date is included in the waste.

rows.under: Polishes a complicated path instead of removing a step.
rows.justRight: Takes out steps until the job is still done and nothing extra remains.
rows.over: Simplifies until the person who needs the result cannot complete it.

rows.situation: A result that is merely fine
rows.under: Ships it and does not ask how it could win, not just finish.
rows.justRight: Asks what would make it clearly better for the customer, and does the one change that fits the date.
rows.over: Holds the result for a leap that misses the date and does not improve what ships.

rows.under: Plans the work as a list of tasks and never asks what winning means.
rows.justRight: Says what winning looks like, in the customer's terms, and checks the plan against it.
rows.over: Rewrites the ambition every few days so the team cannot deliver any version of it.

rows.under: Calls done as soon as it runs, including the parts a customer would trip on.
rows.justRight: Sets the bar for this delivery, hits it, and writes down the improvement that waits until next time.
rows.over: Keeps perfecting past the bar you set, and the delivery moves.

rows.situation: A path the customer could choose instead
rows.under: Ignores the other way they could get the job done.
rows.justRight: Looks at that alternative and changes one thing so your path is the better one.
rows.over: Copies the alternative feature for feature and loses the date and the point.

rows.situation: The first version is not the win
rows.under: Treats the first version as the finished ambition.
rows.justRight: Ships a version that teaches you something, with a dated next step toward the win.
rows.over: Refuses to ship until the full ambition is in the first version.

rows.situation: Raising the bar on a date
rows.under: Lowers the bar quietly so the date is easy.
rows.justRight: Keeps the date and raises one part of the result that the customer will actually feel.
rows.over: Raises every part of the bar and then misses the date you promised.

rows.under: Leaves the goal as a phrase and lets each person invent a project.
rows.justRight: Turns it into the outcome, the owner, and the first week of work before the meeting ends.
rows.over: Writes a plan so detailed it pretends the uncertainty is already gone.

rows.under: Staffs all three because they were said out loud.
rows.justRight: Names the thread they share and picks one execution plan.
rows.over: Forces a merger that keeps every idea's scope, so nothing got more concrete.

rows.under: Ends the discussion with a shared sense of progress and no name on the work.
rows.justRight: Writes the next three steps, who does each, and the date of the first one.
rows.over: Assigns an owner to every hypothetical branch, including ones you will not hit.

rows.situation: The team is stuck in ambiguity
rows.under: Tells people to get comfortable with ambiguity and adds no plan.
rows.justRight: Separates what is known, what is a guess, and the next action that would reduce the guess.
rows.over: Demands certainty before anyone may move, which freezes the week.

rows.situation: A discussion that should become work
rows.under: Schedules another discussion.
rows.justRight: Leaves with a one-page plan the team can start tomorrow.
rows.over: Produces a long document nobody will run, and calls the document the plan.

rows.under: Keeps the idea vague so you cannot be wrong.
rows.justRight: Puts a number, a date, and a scope on it, and marks which figures are still guesses.
rows.over: Publishes exact figures you have not earned, and the team plans around fiction.

rows.under: Treats the late nights as the plan for the next month.
rows.justRight: Finishes the spike, then cuts the following week's load so the team can sustain the pace.
rows.over: Cancels the spike entirely and calls rest a strategy while the commitment slips with no warning.

rows.under: Starts the push already depleted and hopes intensity will appear.
rows.justRight: Clears the calendar, says how long the push is, and protects sleep and one real stop.
rows.over: Prepares so carefully that the push never starts.

rows.under: Says yes to each one and the long-term work dies in the noise.
rows.justRight: Takes the urgent thread that truly cannot wait and names the ones that will wait until next week.
rows.over: Refuses every urgent thread to protect a plan, including the one that would stop the team.

rows.under: Schedules the next spike on top of the last one.
rows.justRight: Puts recovery on the calendar and uses it, then returns to a pace you can repeat.
rows.over: Takes a recovery so long that the team loses the momentum the spike created.

rows.under: Looks busy and does not manage the energy the work will actually take.
rows.justRight: Matches effort to the real duration of the work, not to how urgent the room sounds.
rows.over: Polices other people's hours as a substitute for your own pace.

rows.under: Ignores the slump and makes worse decisions as the week goes on.
rows.justRight: Notices the slump, changes the order of the work, and asks for help on the piece that can move.
rows.over: Makes the team's pace revolve around your energy and calls that sustainability.

rows.under: Keeps it because stopping it would disappoint people.
rows.justRight: Stops it in public, says what the team is choosing to win instead, and moves the people.
rows.over: Kills it so abruptly that in-flight commitments to customers are part of the wreckage.

rows.under: Funds all of them a little so nobody has to lose.
rows.justRight: Picks the one or two that must win and gives them enough to move this month.
rows.over: Picks one and refuses a small bet that protects it, such as the fix that keeps the current product alive.

rows.under: Adds the wanted work beside the necessary work and hopes both fit.
rows.justRight: Says no, writes down what you are giving up, and does not reopen it this week.
rows.over: Says no to the work that is the actual win because it is less exciting.

rows.situation: A roadmap that is a wish list
rows.under: Publishes every idea as if it were a commitment.
rows.justRight: Marks what will happen, what will not, and what would have to be true to reopen it.
rows.over: Cuts the list so hard that the team has no next step after the current week.

rows.under: Waits for someone senior to kill the extra work.
rows.justRight: Recommends the cut yourself, with what it costs and what it saves.
rows.over: Announces cuts you have not thought through, to look decisive.

rows.under: Starts executing five things quickly and calls the motion focus.
rows.justRight: Cuts the list first, then moves fast on what remains.
rows.over: Spends the month debating the cut and never executes the winner.

rows.under: Says it is not your job and walks past it.
rows.justRight: Raises it to the people who own it, with what you have seen, and stays available for the part you can actually do.
rows.over: Takes over the other department's problem and leaves your own undone.

rows.situation: A local win that hurts the next team
rows.under: Takes the local win and lets the next team discover the cost.
rows.justRight: Shows the downstream cost and picks the option that is better for the whole company, even if your number looks worse.
rows.over: Blocks every local improvement in the name of a global view you have not checked.

rows.under: Absorbs the upstream mess and complains later.
rows.justRight: Goes upstream with the specific defect and the effect on your customers, and agrees a change.
rows.over: Dictates the upstream team's priorities as if their whole job were your input.

rows.under: Uses the phrase, or the polite version of it, and the customer waits.
rows.justRight: Does the next useful step or finds the person who will, and does not leave the problem in the gap.
rows.over: Collects other people's jobs until you are the bottleneck you meant to avoid.

rows.under: Chooses the metric that makes your team look best this month.
rows.justRight: Chooses the metric the company would pick if it could see what you see.
rows.over: Ignores your own commitments and calls every local goal selfish.

rows.under: Turns another team away from a problem that crosses the boundary.
rows.justRight: Lets them in for the part that affects them, and keeps a clear owner for the decision.
rows.over: Invites every team into every decision so the kitchen has no cook.

rows.under: Patches it again and does not ask why the first patch failed.
rows.justRight: Fixes the customer impact, then adds the one check that would have caught this cause.
rows.over: Opens a program to prevent every class of defect and the current one stays open.

rows.under: Ships the fix and relies on someone remembering next time.
rows.justRight: Adds a small check, a test, or a step in the process that runs without heroics.
rows.over: Adds a review board for a problem a single automated check would catch.

rows.situation: A process nobody can run twice
rows.under: Depends on one person who knows the trick.
rows.justRight: Writes the process so a second person can run it, and watches them do it once.
rows.over: Documents every branch until nobody will read it, and the hero remains the process.

rows.under: Learns about the defect from a customer weeks after the next batch has shipped.
rows.justRight: Puts a signal where the work happens, so the next run can change.
rows.over: Builds a dashboard nobody checks and calls the mechanism done.

rows.under: Only prevents, and the people already hit by the defect are still stuck.
rows.justRight: Fixes the people who are stuck now, then spends the next slice on the cause.
rows.over: Only fixes, and schedules the same incident for next month.

rows.situation: A mechanism that becomes the job
rows.under: Has no mechanism, only a promise to be more careful.
rows.justRight: Adds the smallest mechanism that changes the next occurrence, and leaves it alone if it works.
rows.over: Keeps adding steps after the defect has stopped, and the process is now the delay.

rows.under: Adds it beside the old path and leaves both.
rows.justRight: Adds it only if it replaces a harder path, and removes that path.
rows.over: Removes the old path before the new one can do the job the customer already does.

rows.under: Ships the setting so you do not have to choose a default.
rows.justRight: Picks the default that fits almost everyone and deletes the setting.
rows.over: Deletes a setting a real group depends on, and calls the deletion simplicity.

rows.situation: A name that needs a paragraph
rows.under: Adds a glossary entry and keeps the name.
rows.justRight: Renames it to what a new person would guess, and updates the one place people look.
rows.over: Renames it every month in the name of clarity, and nobody can find the old notes.

rows.situation: Five steps that could be two
rows.under: Optimizes each step and leaves the count alone.
rows.justRight: Cuts the path to the two steps that change the outcome.
rows.over: Collapses the path into one step that hides a decision the person needed to make.

rows.under: Walks past a tangled path because you did not create it.
rows.justRight: Simplifies the part you are touching anyway, and leaves a note on the rest.
rows.over: Rewrites the whole area while you were only there to change one thing.

rows.situation: Simple for you, worse for the customer
rows.under: Makes the internal workflow tidy and adds steps for the customer.
rows.justRight: Judges simplicity by the customer's path, including the support burden it creates.
rows.over: Strips the product until it is simple and no longer does the job.

rows.situation: A team you do not manage
rows.under: Escalates to their boss as the first move.
rows.justRight: Writes the idea, the evidence, and what you need, and asks them to decide.
rows.over: Works the room until a reluctant yes appears, and the evidence was never the point.

rows.under: Opens with who you are instead of what you know.
rows.justRight: Opens with the insight and lets the argument carry the ask.
rows.over: Hides a weak argument behind a humble tone and still expects the title to finish it.

rows.under: Calls a meeting because you have not made the idea clear yet.
rows.justRight: Sends a short writeup first, and uses the meeting only for the decision.
rows.over: Sends a long document and treats silence as alignment.

rows.under: Buries the data because the senior person has already spoken.
rows.justRight: Shows the data, says what decision it supports, and accepts the call if they still disagree for a stated reason.
rows.over: Uses the data as a weapon and keeps score after the decision.

rows.under: Mentions it once in a channel and moves on.
rows.justRight: States the insight, who it is for, and the decision it should change.
rows.over: Campaigns for the insight after the decision has gone another way.

rows.under: Defers because you are junior, even when you have the fact.
rows.justRight: Puts the fact in front of the decision and does not pretend the org chart is the evidence.
rows.over: Treats every position as illegitimate and will not follow a decision you lost.

rows.under: Finishes the old plan because changing it would admit the plan was wrong.
rows.justRight: Changes the next slice to the new need and says what you are dropping.
rows.over: Chases the new request so fast that nothing already promised gets finished.

rows.under: Tells them the roadmap is the roadmap.
rows.justRight: Asks what they now need this month, and moves one commitment to meet it.
rows.over: Rebuilds the whole plan around one partner and your other customers wait.

rows.under: Keeps staffing it after the customer signal has turned.
rows.justRight: Stops or shrinks it, and moves the people onto the bet the signal now supports.
rows.over: Kills it on the first quiet week, before you know whether the signal is real.

rows.situation: A change that is only internal
rows.under: Calls an internal reorganization a customer response.
rows.justRight: Checks that the change removes a wait, a defect, or a step the customer feels.
rows.over: Refuses every internal improvement, including one that would let you adapt faster next time.

rows.under: Schedules the response for the next planning cycle by default.
rows.justRight: Responds this week with a small change, and saves the larger redesign for when you understand it.
rows.over: Promises a full new solution in the same week and misses both the promise and the current job.

rows.under: Ships the original plan long after the customer has moved on.
rows.justRight: Ships the adapted slice on the date you reset, and tells the customer what changed.
rows.over: Resets the plan every few days, so the team never ships either version.

rows.under: Goes dark, or snaps, and leaves the team to guess how bad it is.
rows.justRight: Names the hard part, stays decent to people, and points at the next useful step.
rows.over: Insists everyone act upbeat and treats a worried question as bad attitude.

rows.under: Moves straight to the next problem and the win disappears.
rows.justRight: Names who did it and what was hard, briefly, then gets back to work.
rows.over: Celebrates so long that the unfinished work becomes someone else's emergency.

rows.under: Leaves them alone because you do not want to make it awkward.
rows.justRight: Offers a specific help, takes a piece if you can, and still expects the work to get done.
rows.over: Takes the work away permanently and calls that support.

rows.under: Pretends the miss did not happen so the mood stays light.
rows.justRight: Says the miss plainly and keeps the tone one a person can work in.
rows.over: Dwells on the miss until the room cannot function.

rows.under: Lets the win pass with no names, so people feel invisible.
rows.justRight: Gives the credit where the work happened, in front of the team.
rows.over: Performs gratitude that praises everyone and informs no one.

rows.under: Uses optimism to avoid saying the project is off track.
rows.justRight: Stays constructive and still puts the risk on the table the day you know it.
rows.over: Polices tone so carefully that bad news arrives late.

rows.under: Sets a target the team can hit without changing how it works.
rows.justRight: Sets a target that requires a real change, and says what support comes with it.
rows.over: Sets a target nobody believes, and does not change the plan that would have to hit it.

rows.under: Says they are doing fine, or says they need to be better, with no example.
rows.justRight: Gives one example, the bar you want, and a chance to try it this week.
rows.over: Delivers a pile of feedback so large they cannot tell what to practice.

rows.under: Protects the comfort and calls stability a high bar.
rows.justRight: Raises one expectation the customer will feel, and coaches the people who are not there yet.
rows.over: Raises every expectation at once and loses the people who were about to get there.

rows.under: Keeps a person who cannot meet the bar and works around them.
rows.justRight: Makes the bar clear, helps them reach it, and moves them if they cannot.
rows.over: Cycles people out so quickly that the bar is a threat instead of a standard.

rows.situation: A goal the team does not believe
rows.under: Repeats the goal louder.
rows.justRight: Shows the path, cuts scope that does not serve it, and asks what would make the goal credible.
rows.over: Lowers the goal at the first doubt and calls the doubt alignment.

rows.under: Announces the bar and leaves people to figure it out alone.
rows.justRight: Pairs the higher bar with time, an example, or a person who has done it.
rows.over: Does the work for them so the result looks raised and they did not grow.

rows.under: Treats the win as proof you should not be questioned.
rows.justRight: Says what worked, what was luck, and what you would change next time.
rows.over: Dismisses the win so completely that the team cannot learn what to repeat.

rows.under: Takes the credit, or fails to notice who else made it possible.
rows.justRight: Names the other people and keeps the part that was actually yours.
rows.over: Refuses any credit, so the people who depend on you cannot tell what you will own next time.

rows.under: Defends the win and misses the useful part of the note.
rows.justRight: Asks what they saw, keeps the part that would make the next one better, and does not grovel.
rows.over: Rewrites the win as a failure to show you can take a note.

rows.under: Says thanks with no content, or says nothing.
rows.justRight: Thanks the specific person for the specific thing, and says what it unlocked.
rows.over: Performs gratitude in public for work you have not actually looked at.
