rows.under: Closes the method because it just worked.
rows.justRight: Asks one person who does it differently what they would change, and tries the part that fits.
rows.over: Abandons a working method at the first alternative.

rows.under: Confuses confidence with arrogance and still needs a decision.
rows.justRight: Decides, and holds the decision lightly enough to update when the evidence changes.
rows.over: Refuses to decide because any choice might look proud.

rows.situation: A teammate stuck on other work
rows.under: Leaves them stuck because it is not your goal.
rows.justRight: Spends a bounded slice of time to unblock them, then returns to your own commitment.
rows.over: Takes over their goal and drops the result you owed.

rows.under: Waits for the official owner, who is not around, while the person stays blocked.
rows.justRight: Answers what you know, says what you do not, and points at the owner for the rest.
rows.over: Answers beyond what you know and sends them down the wrong path with confidence.

rows.under: Keeps a task that someone else needs to touch, because sharing it would slow you today.
rows.justRight: Shares the context and lets them do the part that is theirs, even if you could finish it faster.
rows.over: Hands off work you have not explained, and calls the dump collaboration.

rows.situation: Help that was not asked for
rows.under: Watches them struggle because they did not ask in the right way.
rows.justRight: Offers once, specifically, and accepts a no.
rows.over: Helps over the refusal and rewrites their work.

rows.under: Helps everyone else and surprises your stakeholders when your goal slips.
rows.justRight: Helps in a way that still lets you warn early if your own date moves.
rows.over: Refuses every request the moment your own date looks tight, including a ten-minute unblock.

rows.situation: Work that crosses into your area
rows.under: Treats their edit as an intrusion.
rows.justRight: Welcomes the useful change, reviews it, and keeps ownership of the outcome.
rows.over: Lets anyone edit anything so you never have to say no, and the result has no owner.

rows.under: Takes the shortcut and leaves the cost with every other team.
rows.justRight: Takes it only if the total time and energy go down, and says who pays if they do not.
rows.over: Bans the shortcut even when it is cheaper for everyone, because it was not invented centrally.

rows.under: Builds a tool that saves your team an hour and costs the community a day of exceptions.
rows.justRight: Uses the shared path, or fixes the shared path, instead of a private one.
rows.over: Forces a global tool that is worse than the local one for every team, including yours.

rows.under: Special-cases one person's workflow and everyone else routes around it.
rows.justRight: Asks whether the change helps the broader group, and declines it when it does not.
rows.over: Refuses a one-person fix that would also remove a trap for everyone else.

rows.under: Saves money and spends a week of people's time to do it, or the reverse, without counting.
rows.justRight: Counts the scarce thing, including time and energy, and picks the cheaper total.
rows.over: Optimizes a spreadsheet while the actual waste is in the work.

rows.under: Rebuilds a novel version because the shared one is dull.
rows.justRight: Uses the boring shared solution and improves it where it fails the broader group.
rows.over: Standardizes on a boring solution that does not do the job, and forbids the fix.

rows.under: Celebrates a local saving that moved the cost one team over.
rows.justRight: Reports the effect on the whole path, not only on your step.
rows.over: Ignores a real local waste because you cannot prove the global number today.

rows.under: Lets the usual voices run the meeting and reads silence as comfort.
rows.justRight: Notices who has not spoken, asks for that view, and makes it safe to give it.
rows.over: Calls on people to represent a category, which puts them on the spot instead of in the work.

rows.situation: A norm that fits one kind of life
rows.under: Sets the hours, the social plan, or the ritual around the people who already fit it.
rows.justRight: Changes the one norm that keeps a teammate from contributing, and keeps the bar on the work.
rows.over: Drops the work expectation so the norm never has to be discussed.

rows.situation: A room that all looks the same
rows.under: Does not notice, or notices and does nothing about how the next person gets in.
rows.justRight: Changes how you source and assess the next seat so the room can include someone the current pattern misses.
rows.over: Hires for the appearance of variety and does not give the person real work.

rows.under: Plans the event around one kind of body, budget, or family situation.
rows.justRight: Asks what would keep people out and changes that part before the invitations go.
rows.over: Cancels every gathering so there is no risk of excluding anyone, and the team never meets.

rows.under: Puts the words on a page and leaves the meeting unchanged.
rows.justRight: Picks one behavior in the week's meetings that will be different, and checks whether it was.
rows.over: Builds a campaign about belonging while the person being talked about is not in the work.

rows.under: Withholds a hard assignment so a person never has to struggle in public.
rows.justRight: Gives the hard assignment with the support to succeed, because contribution is what belonging is for.
rows.over: Uses the assignment as a test they are expected to fail.

rows.situation: A big change that could be a slice
rows.under: Builds the whole thing before anyone uses it.
rows.justRight: Ships the smallest slice that a real user can complete, and learns from that.
rows.over: Ships a slice so thin that the user cannot do the job, and calls the confusion learning.

rows.situation: Feedback from the people who use it
rows.under: Asks the team what they think and never asks a user.
rows.justRight: Puts the slice in front of a user, or uses it yourself as they would, and changes the next slice.
rows.over: Rewrites the slice after every comment, including comments that do not bear on the goal.

rows.under: Breaks the path people already rely on so the iteration can move faster.
rows.justRight: Keeps the current path working and adds the slice beside it until the new one is ready.
rows.over: Preserves every old path forever and the iteration never replaces anything.

rows.under: Starts the next slice before you know whether this one worked.
rows.justRight: Names what would prove the slice worked, checks that, and only then continues.
rows.over: Demands statistical certainty from a handful of uses and stalls.

rows.under: Polishes an internal detail and calls it an iteration.
rows.justRight: Chooses a step that answers a real question about the end goal.
rows.over: Makes the step so large that the feedback arrives after the design is frozen.

rows.under: Ships to users a thing the team has not tried to use.
rows.justRight: Uses it for a real task first, fixes the break you hit, and then asks others.
rows.over: Refuses to show users anything until the team is fully satisfied with it.

rows.situation: A decision in a private chat
rows.under: Leaves the decision in the private thread and wonders why others redo it.
rows.justRight: Moves the decision to a place the people who need it can read, and links the reason.
rows.over: Pastes a private conversation, including asides that were never meant to be shared.

rows.situation: A project only the team can see
rows.under: Defaults to a private project because that is easier.
rows.justRight: Makes it public unless there is a concrete reason not to, and writes that reason down.
rows.over: Makes public a project that contains customer data or a personnel matter.

rows.under: Asks for contributions and keeps the context in your head.
rows.justRight: Publishes the goal, the status, and how to propose a change.
rows.over: Publishes so much unfinished noise that contributing is harder than asking you.

rows.situation: A real reason to stay private
rows.under: Uses privacy as the habit, not as a reason.
rows.justRight: Keeps private what would hurt a customer, a person, or an unannounced commitment, and makes the rest public.
rows.over: Announces that everything is public and then hides the actual decision anyway.

rows.under: Files it where only your team will see it.
rows.justRight: Files it in the public tracker with enough detail that someone outside the team could help.
rows.over: Files a vague public issue and then ignores the people who show up.

rows.under: Leaves a public doc you know is stale because correcting it is awkward.
rows.justRight: Corrects it in public and says what changed.
rows.over: Deletes the history so the mistake is harder to see than the fix.

rows.under: Talks about the other site, team, or project as the obstacle.
rows.justRight: Names the shared goal and the specific handoff, and drops the us-and-them wording.
rows.over: Polices other people's wording and never fixes the handoff.

rows.under: Keeps it inside the team because they did not ask yet.
rows.justRight: Sends it to the people who will trip on it, before they trip.
rows.over: Broadcasts every detail to every group and the signal disappears.

rows.situation: Asking when you do not know
rows.under: Guesses, or waits, because asking would cross a boundary.
rows.justRight: Asks the person who knows, wherever they sit, and shares the answer back.
rows.over: Asks so many groups that you create a second project out of the question.

rows.situation: A silo that formed on its own
rows.under: Treats the silo as inevitable and routes around it.
rows.justRight: Puts one regular touch in place with the other group and uses it for a real decision.
rows.over: Dissolves every working group in the name of unity, and the work loses its owners.

rows.situation: A win told as only yours
rows.under: Reports the win as your team's, and leaves out the group that made it possible.
rows.justRight: Reports it as a shared result and says what each side did.
rows.over: Refuses to name any team, so nobody knows who to ask next time.

rows.under: Celebrates your date and ignores that the other group will miss theirs because of you.
rows.justRight: Moves your date, or your scope, when that is what keeps the joint outcome intact.
rows.over: Holds your work until every other group is ready, including groups this release does not need.

rows.under: Misses it and lets people find out when the work is not there.
rows.justRight: Tells them as soon as you know, with the new date you can actually hold.
rows.over: Sends daily warnings before you know anything, and they stop reading them.

rows.under: Leaves the goal undated because the date would be uncomfortable.
rows.justRight: Puts a date on it, or a date for when the date will be set, and writes it where stakeholders look.
rows.over: Invents a date you have no plan to hit, so the surprise is merely delayed.

rows.under: Waits for the date itself, hoping you will recover.
rows.justRight: Says it the day you know, including what will still arrive and what will not.
rows.over: Declares a slip at the first hard day, before you know whether the date is actually lost.

rows.under: Saves the bad news for the meeting so you can explain it live.
rows.justRight: Sends the news before the meeting, and uses the meeting to decide what to do.
rows.over: Sends a flood of minor updates so the one real surprise is harder to see.

rows.under: Says you will know later and does not say when.
rows.justRight: Commits to the day you will either give the date or explain what is still unknown.
rows.over: Schedules a meeting to schedule the meeting, and calls that a date.

rows.under: Quietly redefines done so the original date looks met.
rows.justRight: Delivers what you named, or renegotiates the meaning of done before the date, not after.
rows.over: Hits the date by handing over something the other person cannot use, with no warning.

rows.situation: A meeting that could be a note
rows.under: Holds the meeting because it is on the calendar.
rows.justRight: Sends the note, asks for the decision in writing, and cancels the meeting.
rows.over: Refuses every meeting, including the one where a decision actually requires the room.

rows.situation: A message that wastes the reader
rows.under: Sends a brain dump and lets three people hunt for the ask.
rows.justRight: Puts the ask, the deadline, and the context they need in the first lines.
rows.over: Over-edits a two-line ask for an hour and the decision window closes.

rows.under: Saves the money and spends a week of people on a problem a purchase would remove.
rows.justRight: Spends the money when the time it gives back is the scarcer resource, and says why.
rows.over: Spends freely and calls every purchase a time saving, including ones that create more work.

rows.under: Schedules the second week as if the first had no cost.
rows.justRight: Treats the second week as exceptional, cuts scope, and puts recovery time on the calendar.
rows.over: Bans any extra hour even when a one-time push would prevent a larger mess.

rows.under: Drops by, calls, and forwards threads before you have made the question clear.
rows.justRight: Does the thinking first, then asks for the smallest slice of their time that you still need.
rows.over: Will not ask at all, and burns your own week on something they could have answered.

rows.situation: Recovery as part of the work
rows.under: Praises the person who skipped recovery and quietly expects the same.
rows.justRight: Plans the recovery when you plan the overtime, and does not treat it as a favor.
rows.over: Protects recovery by slipping a commitment you could have reduced in scope instead.

rows.situation: A cheap version that does not work
rows.under: Ships the lean version and leaves the user with a result that is not fit for the job.
rows.justRight: Spends what the job actually requires, and nothing past that.
rows.over: Rebuilds it lavishly because the first version was embarrassing, past the point of fit.

rows.under: Adds finish the job does not need because the lean version feels exposed.
rows.justRight: Stops when it is fit for purpose and writes down what you refused to add.
rows.over: Calls every finish waste, including the one a user needs to complete the task.

rows.under: Picks lean or polished and does not say what you gave up.
rows.justRight: Says what fit for purpose requires here, and what you are leaving out on purpose.
rows.over: Debates the philosophy and does not decide the scope.

rows.under: Keeps refining after it already does the job and nothing more is needed.
rows.justRight: Does one more pass only for a gap a real user would hit, then stops.
rows.over: Stops at the first draft and calls the gaps a style.

rows.under: Saves the effort and hands the user the sharp edge.
rows.justRight: Spends the effort on the edge the user touches, and stays lean everywhere else.
rows.over: Pads every edge and the work is no longer lean or late.

rows.under: Reuses a scrappy shortcut in a place where the purpose is unforgiving.
rows.justRight: Matches the effort to this purpose, which may mean more care than the last job needed.
rows.over: Applies the most careful standard from the last job to a throwaway experiment.

rows.under: Falls in love with the method and does not check whether the customer can feel the result.
rows.justRight: Uses the method only as far as it makes the product better, and stops there.
rows.over: Drops a method that is working because it is not interesting anymore.

rows.under: Extends the study after it has already answered the product question.
rows.justRight: Ends the study when the product decision is clear, and writes down the decision.
rows.over: Skips the study and guesses, then calls the guess customer love.

rows.under: Spends the review on the technique and never asks what the user will do.
rows.justRight: Starts from the user's job and lets the method defend itself only where it changes that job.
rows.over: Bans the method because it looks like research, even where it is the right tool.

rows.situation: Science in service of the product
rows.under: Treats rigor as a distraction from shipping.
rows.justRight: Uses the rigor to choose a design the customer will love, then ships that design.
rows.over: Ships the research notes instead of the product change.

rows.situation: Keeping the customer in the room
rows.under: Debates the model after the customer's pain is already obvious.
rows.justRight: Names the customer pain, then picks the smallest rigorous step that would address it.
rows.over: Quotes the customer and skips the thinking that would turn the quote into a product.

rows.situation: A shortcut that hurts the product
rows.under: Takes a sloppy shortcut and hopes the customer will not notice.
rows.justRight: Takes a shortcut only if the product the customer touches still holds up.
rows.over: Refuses every shortcut, including one that would get a better product to them sooner.

rows.under: Wraps an experiment in the full release process and learns nothing this month.
rows.justRight: Uses a light process, labels the work as early, and keeps it away from the certified path.
rows.over: Treats the experiment as if a failure would be harmless in the certified system.

rows.situation: A certified change treated as a sketch
rows.under: Edits a certified system with the habits of a prototype.
rows.justRight: Uses the checks that system requires, and does not borrow speed from the research bench.
rows.over: Adds research-grade ceremony on top of the certified checks and misses the real gate.

rows.under: Uses whichever habit you used last, regardless of which world this task is in.
rows.justRight: Says which world this task is in before you start, and switches habits on purpose.
rows.over: Writes a new process for the switch and spends the week on the process.

rows.situation: A process from the wrong world
rows.under: Copies the certified checklist into the lab, or the lab's shortcuts into the certified line.
rows.justRight: Keeps a short list of what differs, and follows the list for this task.
rows.over: Maintains two full process empires and makes people serve the process instead of the work.

rows.under: Applies one rigor to every task because it is simpler to remember.
rows.justRight: Raises the rigor when the harm of being wrong goes up, and lowers it when you are still learning.
rows.over: Argues about the classification for longer than the task would have taken.

rows.under: Reports an experiment and a certified result in the same breath, as if they were the same kind of evidence.
rows.justRight: Labels which is which, every time, including in the summary a leader will skim.
rows.over: Separates them so aggressively that a lesson from the lab is not allowed to inform the product.

rows.under: Chooses the finalist with the same background and the same way of thinking. The finalist who would do the job better does not get the offer.
rows.justRight: Chooses the finalist who will do this role best, and says which parts of the work decided it.
rows.over: Chooses the weaker finalist so the team will look more varied on paper.

rows.under: Treats a shared background and the same skills as proof they can do the job. The interviews never test the work.
rows.justRight: Tests the work. A shared background is not a reason to hire them, and it is not a reason to pass.
rows.over: Rejects them for sharing that background, even though they are the best person for the role.

rows.situation: A gap in the first month
rows.under: Waves off a real gap because the candidate will be easy to manage. The team finds the gap after the offer.
rows.justRight: Names the gap, asks whether this person is still the best choice for the role, and hires only if the answer is yes.
rows.over: Hires them with the gap because a target says the next person should change how the team looks. Other people then do the work the role was opened to do.

rows.under: Asks only people who share the hiring manager's background, thinking style, and skills to do the interviews. Every vote repeats the same narrow judgment.
rows.justRight: Asks people who can test the role, including someone whose skills differ, and still decides on who can do the job.
rows.over: Picks interviewers so the panel will hit a target for who should be in the room. A strong candidate gets a no, and the work was never the question.

rows.situation: A referral from your own circle
rows.under: Moves the referral ahead because they come from the same places and think the same way. Someone who might do the job better waits.
rows.justRight: Runs the same bar as any other candidate. The referral gets the offer only if they are the best person for the role.
rows.over: Sets aside a strong referral so the team will not look narrower, and offers the role to someone less able to do it.

rows.under: Writes the role as a copy of the manager: the same background and the same skills. People who could do the work better never match the posting.
rows.justRight: Writes the work the role must do, then hires the best person who can do that work.
rows.over: Writes the role as a slot in a target for how the team should look. The posting describes the look, not the work.

rows.under: Builds a team with the same background, the same thinking style, and the same skills as the manager. The same blind spots show up in every review, and nobody in the room catches them.
rows.justRight: Hires the best person for each role. The set of roles covers more than one background, style, and skill when that is what the outcome needs.
rows.over: Sets a target for how the team should look and accepts a weaker hire to hit it. The team under-delivers because it was not built for the outcome.

rows.under: Hires again from the same background and the same skills after the team misses the same kind of problem. The next person would have missed it too.
rows.justRight: Names the judgment or the skill the team lacks, then hires the best person who can close that gap and still do the role.
rows.over: Adds someone who changes how the team looks on paper and does not have the missing skill. The miss happens again.

rows.under: Hires people who decide the way the manager decides. A bad call gets no pushback until a customer feels it.
rows.justRight: Includes styles that challenge the default, because the outcome is better when the room is not one temperament.
rows.over: Collects contrasting styles to hit a target for how the room looks. The meeting never reaches the decision the business needed.

rows.under: Fills every seat with the skill the manager already has. Work that needs a different skill is done badly, or not done.
rows.justRight: Looks at the outcome the team owes, then fills the missing skill with the best person who has it.
rows.over: Gives up a needed skill to hit a mix on paper. The outcome slips, and the team does not call that a hiring miss.

rows.under: Plans the next hires as more people the manager already trusts, which means people like the manager.
rows.justRight: Plans each seat against the work the outcome needs. The person who gets the seat is the best one for that work, including when the work needs a background, a style, or a skill the team does not have.
rows.over: Assigns the next three hires to a quota. Capable people are passed over when they miss the slot, and less capable people are hired when they fill it.

rows.under: Blames the miss on not having enough people who already work the manager's way, and hires more of them.
rows.justRight: Asks what the outcome needed that the team could not do, and whether the people in the seats could do the work.
rows.over: Hires again to change how the team looks. The result does not improve, because the new person still cannot do the work.

rows.under: Keeps the work to themselves, or leaves people nearby but unsynchronized.
rows.justRight: Pulls the people who are needed, names the shared direction, and keeps them moving together.
rows.over: Invites the whole org so nobody feels left out, and the work has no owner.

rows.under: Lets both run until the join-up fails.
rows.justRight: Gets them onto one direction after the useful disagreement has been heard.
rows.over: Kills the second plan before anyone can say what it knew.

rows.under: Treats the disagreement as a problem to shut down.
rows.justRight: Uses the useful part, then lands a direction the team can run.
rows.over: Keeps the argument open after the call so nobody can start.

rows.situation: A note while the work can still change
rows.under: Saves the critique for the review, when it is expensive.
rows.justRight: Gives the specific gap now, in the spirit of helping the person and the team.
rows.over: Critiques in real time so constantly that people stop showing unfinished work.

rows.situation: Feedback that could land as an attack
rows.under: Softens it until the person cannot tell what to change.
rows.justRight: Is direct about the work, not the person, and stays until the next step is clear.
rows.over: Uses helping the team as cover for a public dressing-down.

rows.under: Withdraws and lets the group guess the plan.
rows.justRight: Shows up, names the load, and keeps the shared direction visible.
rows.over: Needs a huddle before every small call, and the week is only meetings.

rows.under: Ignores it until the two paths collide.
rows.justRight: Pulls them back to the shared direction, or changes the direction if they are right.
rows.over: Polices small differences of method that do not change the outcome.

rows.situation: A team that is only a set of jobs
rows.under: Staffs the seats and hopes a team appears.
rows.justRight: Pulls the people in those seats onto one direction, and judges the result as a group.
rows.over: Blends every role so thoroughly that nobody is accountable for a piece.

rows.under: Waits them out and restates the plan. They can tell they were not heard.
rows.justRight: Listens all the way through, and changes the plan when they are right.
rows.over: Agrees so the meeting stays pleasant, and the decision is mush.

rows.situation: A fact challenges a strong view
rows.under: Defends the view because it is theirs. The fact sits unused.
rows.justRight: Examines the conviction. Keeps it only if it still holds after the fact.
rows.over: Drops a sound view at the first challenge so they look open-minded.

rows.under: Treats the agreement as proof. Nobody goes looking for a missing view.
rows.justRight: Asks for a viewpoint the room does not already have, and uses it if it changes the work.
rows.over: Collects extra views as a ritual and never lets them change the decision.

rows.situation: An idea from outside the usual group
rows.under: Dismisses it because of who brought it. The idea is never tested.
rows.justRight: Hears the idea on its merits. Keeps the part that is new and useful.
rows.over: Adopts it because it is different, without checking whether it is better.

rows.under: Closes the question before the other views have been heard.
rows.justRight: Stays open long enough to learn, then takes a position people can follow.
rows.over: Stays open so long that nobody can tell what they believe.

rows.under: Pushes back on the messenger. The next hard fact arrives late.
rows.justRight: Makes it safe to bring the fact, checks it, and changes course if it holds.
rows.over: Treats the first contrary account as settled, and an unchecked claim becomes the plan.

rows.under: Will not reopen it. Newer people stop bringing evidence.
rows.justRight: Reopens it when the evidence is real, with enough humility to be wrong in public.
rows.over: Reopens every old call so often that the team cannot rely on a decision.

rows.under: Asks only the people who already see the problem the same way.
rows.justRight: Brings in a different viewpoint, because that friction is where a novel idea shows up.
rows.over: Invites every viewpoint and will not rank them, so the discussion never becomes a decision.

rows.situation: A shortcut that touches a hazard
rows.under: Takes the shortcut and leaves the hazard on someone else's checklist.
rows.justRight: Names the hazard, refuses the shortcut, and escalates until a real owner has the risk.
rows.over: Blocks every shortcut nearby, including ones that do not touch the hazard, and the work stops for no safety gain.

rows.situation: Schedule pressure on a safety check
rows.under: Moves the check to after the date so the milestone still holds.
rows.justRight: Keeps the check in front of the date, and holds the work if the check is not done.
rows.over: Adds extra checks that do not cover the hazard, and the date slips with no safety gain.

rows.situation: A known risk about to go forward
rows.under: Sends the work and plans to catch the risk later.
rows.justRight: Holds that work until the risk is mitigated or explicitly accepted by the person who can accept it.
rows.over: Holds unrelated work that has no named hazard, and calls the hold safety.

rows.situation: Cost pressure on a safety step
rows.under: Cuts the step to save the cost and does not say what hazard that step covered.
rows.justRight: Keeps the step when it is what makes the work safe, and looks for a cheaper way that still covers the same hazard.
rows.over: Refuses every cheaper option, even one that covers the same hazard, and the cost becomes the reason nothing ships.

rows.under: Assumes the checklist owner will catch it, and does not look at the item their own work can make unsafe.
rows.justRight: Checks the items their work can make unsafe, and leaves the rest with the owner.
rows.over: Takes over the whole checklist and becomes the bottleneck for work they do not understand.

rows.under: Says it feels unsafe and stops, without saying what could hurt someone.
rows.justRight: Names the hazard, the consequence, and the smallest hold that covers it.
rows.over: Keeps the hold after the hazard is named and covered, because stopping felt safer than deciding.

rows.situation: Skipping a safety step for convenience
rows.under: Skips the step because it is inconvenient and the last few times were fine.
rows.justRight: Does the step when skipping it would put a person or the hardware at risk, and drops a step that no longer covers a real hazard.
rows.over: Keeps every old step, including ones that no longer match the hardware, and the team works around them.

rows.under: Mentions the risk once and goes back to the schedule.
rows.justRight: Escalates until the risk has an owner and a next step, then returns to the work that is still safe to do.
rows.over: Escalates every discomfort as a stop, and the people who own the real risks stop listening.

rows.under: Fills it with someone available who will not raise the work.
rows.justRight: Waits for someone who is great at the work and makes colleagues better, and says what great means for this seat.
rows.over: Leaves the seat empty so long that the people carrying the load start to leave.

rows.situation: A pleasant team shipping average work
rows.under: Protects the mood and leaves the bar alone.
rows.justRight: Treats the average result as the problem, and keeps the team kind while the bar moves.
rows.over: Turns kindness into a suspicion and scores every friendly week as a miss.

rows.situation: Someone loved who is wrong for the seat
rows.under: Keeps them because the relationship is good.
rows.justRight: Moves them when the seat needs someone else, and does it with a straight explanation.
rows.over: Cycles people out to look rigorous, including the person who is still right.

rows.situation: Strong people who do not help each other
rows.under: Accepts the solo output and ignores the handoffs.
rows.justRight: Expects them to make the joint work better, and coaches the specific handoff that is failing.
rows.over: Adds so much joint ceremony that the strong people stop doing the work.

rows.under: Leads with perks and does not talk about who is here.
rows.justRight: Leads with the people. Mentions perks only as a side fact.
rows.over: Refuses a basic tool because talking about anything but the roster feels impure.

rows.situation: Someone describes the team as a family
rows.under: Agrees, and then cannot explain what happens when the work needs a different person.
rows.justRight: Says the team is here to do excellent work together, and that belonging is not the same as unconditional tenure.
rows.over: Uses the sports metaphor to skip ordinary loyalty to people who are still excellent.

rows.situation: A better idea that is not yours
rows.under: Argues yours back into the plan.
rows.justRight: Switches to the better idea and names the person who had it.
rows.over: Drops a good idea of your own so you cannot be accused of self-interest.

rows.situation: Your team's goal against a company outcome
rows.under: Optimizes the team score.
rows.justRight: Takes the company outcome when it is real, and tells the team what changed.
rows.over: Invokes the company to take work your team was not the right group to do.

rows.situation: A colleague stuck on something you can unblock
rows.under: Stays heads-down.
rows.justRight: Unblocks them, then returns to your own commitment.
rows.over: Becomes the permanent helper and your commitment slips.

rows.under: Lets the story center on you.
rows.justRight: Puts the credit where the work happened.
rows.over: Hides your own contribution so completely that the next staffing decision is blind.

rows.situation: You know something the room needs
rows.under: Stays quiet to look humble.
rows.justRight: Says it, and updates it if a better fact shows up.
rows.over: Agrees with each speaker in turn and never states a view.

rows.situation: Help that will miss your own date
rows.under: Either refuses all help, or helps and misses the date in silence.
rows.justRight: Helps when the company is better for it, and renegotiates your date out loud.
rows.over: Renegotiates every date into someone else's problem.

rows.under: Kills it for being unfamiliar.
rows.justRight: Tests the part that might be better, and keeps the current approach until the new one earns the switch.
rows.over: Switches to it because it is new.

rows.situation: A solution that works and is not very good
rows.under: Stops.
rows.justRight: Keeps pushing for a more innovative one without withholding the working version from the people who need it.
rows.over: Withholds the working version for a cleverer one nobody asked for.

rows.situation: An original attempt that is failing
rows.under: Abandons it at the first critique.
rows.justRight: Persists while the evidence is mixed, and stops when it is not.
rows.over: Persists after the evidence is clear, because the idea was original.

rows.situation: An idea from outside the craft
rows.under: Ignores the speaker.
rows.justRight: Judges the idea on the work, and says when the craft still knows better.
rows.over: Prefers the outside idea because it is outside.

rows.situation: Creative work that is not your taste
rows.under: Blocks it.
rows.justRight: Asks whether it is good for the audience it is for.
rows.over: Refuses every quality bar so that taste cannot be challenged.

rows.situation: A week with room for one experiment
rows.under: Spends it on the safe increment, or on three experiments that cannot finish.
rows.justRight: Spends it on the experiment most likely to change the result, and finishes it.
rows.over: Spends it on the most unusual idea with no path to a result.

rows.under: You bluff.
rows.justRight: You say so, and you name the next step that would inform you.
rows.over: You announce uncertainty about things you do know, so nobody can rely on you.

rows.situation: A bet that might fail in public
rows.under: You sand it down until it cannot fail or matter.
rows.justRight: You take it when excellence requires it, and you name how you will know it failed.
rows.over: You take it so you can be seen taking it.

rows.situation: The usual way is blocking excellent work
rows.under: You leave it.
rows.justRight: You challenge the specific part that is in the way, with a better proposal.
rows.over: You challenge the usual way as a personality.

rows.situation: The truth makes you look bad
rows.under: You bury it.
rows.justRight: You put it on the table so the decision can use it.
rows.over: You confess something that does not change the decision.

rows.under: You agree in the room.
rows.justRight: You say it in the room, about the work.
rows.over: You pick the disagreement that will be most visible.

rows.situation: Risk that does not serve the result
rows.under: You take it because risk feels brave.
rows.justRight: You skip it. Courage here is in pursuit of excellence, not of danger.
rows.over: You build a case that every cautious path is cowardice.

rows.under: You keep the old plan.
rows.justRight: You adapt the plan and tell the people who were counting on the old one.
rows.over: You adapt before the change is real.

rows.under: You wait until it is made for you.
rows.justRight: You decide without a long delay, on the facts you have.
rows.over: You decide before you have looked at the facts already on the table.

rows.under: You look for an easier substitute.
rows.justRight: You take it and name the first step.
rows.over: You choose a harder version that does not improve the result.

rows.under: You stop, or you pretend it was nothing.
rows.justRight: You say what broke and take the next useful step the same week.
rows.over: You perform a recovery and skip the repair.

rows.situation: A bad week on a good bet
rows.under: You abandon the bet.
rows.justRight: You stay through the bump, with a date to reconsider if it is a wall.
rows.over: You stay after you know it is a wall.

rows.situation: People already heard the old plan
rows.under: You switch quietly and let them find out.
rows.justRight: You say what changed and what did not.
rows.over: You re-announce a new plan every day.

rows.situation: Would you fight to keep them
rows.under: You do not ask until they quit.
rows.justRight: You ask while they are here, and you act on the answer.
rows.over: You ask it as a threat.

rows.under: You answer from how hard the seat is to fill this month.
rows.justRight: You answer from the role as it is now, and the whole record.
rows.over: You answer from one bad month.

rows.situation: They do not know where they stand
rows.under: You save it for a formal cycle.
rows.justRight: You talk about what is going well and what is not, regularly.
rows.over: You deliver a weekly verdict and they cannot hear a real signal.

rows.situation: A bet that did not pay off
rows.under: You let that bet decide.
rows.justRight: You weigh it with the rest of the record, including bets that were worth making.
rows.over: You ignore a pattern because an old win is still listed.

rows.under: You treat the bump as the keeper-test answer.
rows.justRight: You stick with them when you would still fight to keep them, and you say what has to change.
rows.over: You cite the bump rule to avoid an answer you already have.

rows.under: You delay the conversation for another quarter.
rows.justRight: You part quickly and fairly, with a clear reason.
rows.over: You part in a way that punishes them for a bet you had asked them to take.

rows.situation: A decision the closest person can make
rows.under: You pull it upward.
rows.justRight: You leave it with them, and you make sure they have the information.
rows.over: You leave them a decision they cannot make, and you are gone.

rows.situation: Information that would change the call
rows.under: You keep it.
rows.justRight: You share it in time, including the uncomfortable part.
rows.over: You forward a pile of documents and call that context.

rows.situation: A process whose original miss is gone
rows.under: You keep it.
rows.justRight: You remove it, unless it still prevents a serious harm.
rows.over: You remove the rule that prevents a serious harm.

rows.under: You wait to be told, or you skip the unglamorous part.
rows.justRight: You act, including the unglamorous part, without a checklist.
rows.over: You invent a checklist for how other people use their freedom.

rows.under: You pride yourself on how many you make.
rows.justRight: You pride yourself on how few you make, and the few are the ones that are actually yours.
rows.over: You make none, including the one only you can make.

rows.situation: A new teammate in an open system
rows.under: You assume they will absorb it.
rows.justRight: You give them the information and the room to decide, and you coach the first calls.
rows.over: You close the system back up because one new person was confused.

rows.situation: The team is about to decide
rows.under: You decide for them, or you vanish.
rows.justRight: You give the context and let them decide.
rows.over: You hint until your preferred answer is the only safe one.

rows.under: You disengage.
rows.justRight: You stay close enough to coach and you do not take the pen.
rows.over: You coach by rewriting.

rows.situation: A decision that is unethical or could materially harm the company
rows.under: You let it go because stepping in feels like control.
rows.justRight: You step in, say why this one is different, and hand the next ordinary call back.
rows.over: You step in whenever you disagree.

rows.situation: A crisis, or a new person without the context
rows.under: You use the same distance you use with a seasoned team on a calm day.
rows.justRight: You step in for the crisis, or until they have the context, and then you step back.
rows.over: You keep the controls for the rest of the quarter.

rows.under: You work the queue.
rows.justRight: You find the context they were missing and stop requiring the approval.
rows.over: You refuse to hear a question even when the context is what they lack.

rows.situation: The team has information and no priority
rows.under: You call the pile context.
rows.justRight: You say what matters and what does not, and you still let them choose the path.
rows.over: You name the priority and then specify every step.

rows.under: A committee owns it, which means nobody does.
rows.justRight: One informed captain owns the judgment call.
rows.over: A captain is named who does not know the work.

rows.situation: Other teams have to carry the decision out
rows.under: Each team reopens the call.
rows.justRight: Each team has a captain for the how, and the what stays decided.
rows.over: You script the how for every team.

rows.situation: Teams that should move without a joint meeting
rows.under: You couple every step, or you let them diverge.
rows.justRight: You keep the aim shared and let the teams operate.
rows.over: You call a lack of communication alignment.

rows.under: The captain shares the blame across everyone who was consulted.
rows.justRight: The captain owns the outcome.
rows.over: The captain owns it so quietly that the other teams never hear the call.

rows.under: You pick the most senior person in the room.
rows.justRight: You pick the person informed enough to make the call, wherever they sit.
rows.over: You pick someone uninformed so the decision will be fast.

rows.under: You treat input as a vote, or you skip it.
rows.justRight: You gather input and the captain still decides.
rows.over: You gather input and then hide the decision.

rows.under: You ask the people who already agree.
rows.justRight: You go find a real disagreement, including one level or team away.
rows.over: You poll so widely that the call never happens.

rows.under: You count heads, or you only hear seniority.
rows.justRight: You give more weight to the craft the decision sits in, and you still hear a sharp outside dissent.
rows.over: You refuse to hear anyone outside the craft.

rows.under: You take the quiet as a yes.
rows.justRight: You ask who disagrees and you wait.
rows.over: You keep asking until someone invents a dissent.

rows.situation: A dissent you will not follow
rows.under: You adopt it to look open, or you punish it.
rows.justRight: You say what you decided and why their point did not carry it.
rows.over: You collect it and never show that you heard it.

rows.situation: A good idea from an unexpected person
rows.under: You skip it because of their level.
rows.justRight: You use it and you name them.
rows.over: You restart the decision for every unexpected comment.

rows.situation: Dissent that arrives after the decision
rows.under: You reopen the call for it, or you scold them for being late.
rows.justRight: You hear whether it is a new fact. If it is not, you hold the decision and thank them.
rows.over: You ban any comment after the decision, including a new fact.

rows.under: You write a rule for everyone.
rows.justRight: You deal with that person. You add a rule only for a harm judgment will not reliably prevent.
rows.over: You refuse a rule against a serious harm.

rows.under: You add it because another company has it.
rows.justRight: You keep it only when it is simple, efficient, and impactful.
rows.over: You reject one that is all three, because the slogan said no rules.

rows.under: You wait for permission, or you vanish.
rows.justRight: You take the vacation and you leave the work covered.
rows.over: You treat people who take vacation as less committed.

rows.under: You expense whatever a form will allow, or you refuse a cost the work needs.
rows.justRight: You spend when it is in the company's interest, and you can say why.
rows.over: You become a private approver for everyone else's judgment.

rows.situation: A rule against harassment, leaking, or insider trading
rows.under: You loosen it in the name of freedom.
rows.justRight: You keep it strict.
rows.over: You wrap it in procedure that catches nobody.

rows.situation: A growing team and a fear of mistakes
rows.under: You add rules to dummy-proof the work.
rows.justRight: You accept some mistakes as the price of judgment, and you do not accept the serious harms.
rows.over: You celebrate mistakes that were just carelessness.

rows.situation: A bold path and a safe path
rows.under: You take the safe path by default.
rows.justRight: You take the bold path when the ambition is real, and you design it so a failure teaches you something.
rows.over: You take the bold path with no way to learn and no owner for the downside.

rows.situation: An experiment people will actually meet
rows.under: You never run it, or you run it without reading the result.
rows.justRight: You run it, read it, and adapt.
rows.over: You run so many that the result cannot be attributed.

rows.under: You let it run to avoid looking uncomfortable.
rows.justRight: You change the method and keep the ambition.
rows.over: You drop the ambition at the first bad week.

rows.under: You pretend the job will calm down.
rows.justRight: You tell them the truth about the pace of bets.
rows.over: You mock the preference.

rows.under: You remove all of it, or you add it for drama.
rows.justRight: You keep the discomfort that is the price of a better result.
rows.over: You add chaos so the work feels important.

rows.situation: The usual approach would be fine and small
rows.under: You repeat it forever, or you discard it because it is usual.
rows.justRight: You look for a different approach when the usual one will not get you to the ambition.
rows.over: You discard a working approach because it is not exciting.

rows.situation: A story that cuts against your values
rows.under: You block it or stall it.
rows.justRight: You support the creator's expression and you do your part of the work.
rows.over: You attack colleagues who are uncomfortable.

rows.situation: Work you perceive as harmful, in a role that touches it
rows.under: You sabotage it, or you refuse the role and stay.
rows.justRight: You do the role, or you say this is the wrong place and you leave the work handable.
rows.over: You require everyone else to enjoy it.

rows.situation: A slate far from your taste
rows.under: You try to narrow it to what you find acceptable.
rows.justRight: You judge a title by the audience it is for.
rows.over: You add titles only to provoke.

rows.situation: A member choosing what to watch or play
rows.under: You hide the advisory, or you scold the choice.
rows.justRight: You give ratings, advisories, and parental controls in the languages they use, and you let them choose.
rows.over: You put every warning on every title until the controls mean nothing.

rows.under: You stay and fight the slate from inside.
rows.justRight: You say so and you leave the work in a state others can carry.
rows.over: You campaign to make the slate match you.

rows.situation: A creator you chose, doing something you would not
rows.under: You try to steer their expression to your taste.
rows.justRight: You support the expression you chose them for.
rows.over: You treat every title as your personal statement.
